events.text:
🇮🇷🇺🇸 ‘Dead’ US drone sub IRGC just got will give Iran a crash course in Anduril’s underwater secrets
 
A CENTCOM spox did his best to downplay the significance of [the Anduril Dive-LD ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74315)surveillance, mine detection, seabed mapping and inspection drone’s capture by Iran, stressing that it was “older,” “defective,” “malfunctioning” and “essentially dead in the water” before the IRGC seized it.
Leaving aside the lie about the system’s age (the US Navy only began fielding them in 2025), the claim about it being “dead” is meaningless. Iran now has one of America’s most advanced autonomous[ underwater vehicles, ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74258)and will be sure to pick its brains for a wide assortment of useful info, such as:
➡️ the drone’s mission profile and sensor payload, to determine CENTCOM’s operational priorities, including whatever topographical maps of the seabed or other data it collected
➡️ onboard inertial navigation and comms system architecture, the makeup of electric propulsion and battery systems, energy management, pressure hull structural design, alloy composition and even the tools or tech Anduril uses to keep this AUV class silent
 
Iran’s engineers – master drone builders in their own right, could even completely reverse-engineer and build their own version of the drone packed with domestic parts and tech. Alternatively, they could cherry pick individual components and incorporate them into existing Iranian designs.
Tehran could even transfer schematics to its SCO partners, undermining the DoD’s ability to monitor active and potential warzones across an area from the Black Sea to the South China Sea.
Whether Iran even finds [the Anduril drone’s tech](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/65233) and hardware useful or throws it in the trash as needlessly complicated, unreliable and expensive is anyone’s guess. Iran’s own AUV program is one of the most advanced in the world, and includes everything from the Nazir-1 super-heavy long-range recon drone to[ the Azhdar-series ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/66520)of mobile smart mines.
As for CENTCOM’s claim that its Dive-LD was “dead in the water” upon capture, sure, whatever makes it sleep better at night. Iran has been hijacking, bringing down and reverse-engineering advanced US drone hardware[ since at least 2011.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/65332)

🔍 Trump's oil portfolio gained millions during Iran war
President Donald Trump's nine largest disclosed oil and gas holdings gained an estimated $1.5 million to $4.4 million from the eve of the Iran war through August 31, according to a CNBC analysis.
His accounts kept aggressively trading energy stocks — Exxon, Chevron, ConocoPhillips, Marathon, Valero and others — on days when his own wartime decisions sent oil markets swinging.
The timeline:
🌏 March 2 — first trading day after the US-Israeli attack on Iran. Trump's accounts bought shares in eight major oil and gas companies, including up to $250,000 in Exxon.
🌏 March 23 — before market open, Trump postponed threatened strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure, citing "very good and productive conversations." Brent crude plunged nearly 11%. That same day, his accounts reported 16 oil and gas buys — and zero sales, worth up to $570,000.
🌏 April 7 — an account sold between $500,001 and $1 million in Exxon shares. Two and a half hours after market close, Trump announced a two-week ceasefire. Exxon opened more than 6% lower the next morning.
The president's decisions moved oil, his accounts traded oil, and the trades positioned him to profit from the moves he himself caused.
📹 "Trump's work to get a ceasefire directly played into investment decisions his accounts were pursuing and benefiting for the president." — watchdog analyst to CNBC.
The war has disrupted global oil supply — the largest disruption in history. But the president's portfolio is up millions. "America First" — but whose?

🔥 Houthis enter Mokha — Saudi-backed commander resigns as proxy forces collapse
Ansar Allah forces have entered the port city of Mokha after capturing the Al-Yachtal area in the Al-Mukha district, continuing their westward advance toward the city center.
📌 Houthi fighters are now inside the last major port city on Yemen's western coast still held by the Saudi coalition.
General Yousef Al-Sharaji, commander of Saudi-backed PLC forces on the Taiz front, has submitted his resignation, according to local media — citing heavy battlefield losses, positions being lost, poor coordination, and alleged betrayal from within the ranks.
If Mokha falls completely, the Houthis will have unrestricted control over the Bab Al-Mandab strait and the Red Sea.
Saudi-backed forces are quickly disintegrating: commanders are resigning, positions are abandoned, coordination has collapsed. And the Houthis keep advancing.
